shots.title: HONEY NEVER SPOILS
shots.purpose: Put the substance itself on trial — dense, golden, alive — before any science arrives
shots.claim: honey found in ancient tombs remains edible after ~3,000 years
shots.evidence: full-bleed amber honey pour plate; the substance is the subject
shots.motion_reason: slow push-in: stillness first so the question lands clean
shots.transition_reason: hard cut to the rot-vs-honey split when the mechanism question opens

subject_contract.expected_subject: a close-up of thick golden honey — slow pour or heavy drip on a dark ground
required: golden-amber honey as the dominant subject
thick viscous texture: pour, drip or swirl
forbidden: bees, hives or honeycomb dominating the frame
pancakes, toast or prepared food dishes

one_second.relationship: the honey itself — pure, dense, alive

shots.purpose: Show the water problem: the same table, two fates — one rots, one doesn't
shots.evidence: split plate: rotting water-rich fruit vs untouched honey
shots.motion_reason: gentle drift across the split so both fates are read
shots.transition_reason: hard cut to the osmosis diagram when the mechanism must be seen

subject_contract.expected_subject: a split composition: rotting water-rich fruit on one side, clean golden honey on the other
required: one side decaying fruit with mould

one_second.relationship: the rot and the honey — same table, different water

shots.purpose: Make the kill mechanism visible: osmotic arrows draining a single cell
shots.claim: supersaturated sugar solution dehydrates microbes by osmosis
shots.evidence: parchment diagram plate: one bacterium in a dense golden field, arrows outward
shots.motion_reason: slow zoom on the cell so the outward arrows read as one idea
shots.transition_reason: cut to the hive when the story asks how the water got removed

subject_contract.expected_subject: a parchment-style scientific diagram: one small round bacterium at the centre of a dense golden field with arrows pointing outward

one_second.relationship: one cell losing its water to the syrup around it

shots.purpose: Show the industry: bees fanning the comb — evaporation as labour
shots.claim: bees evaporate nectar from ~70-80% water down to 17-18% honey
shots.evidence: worker bees on comb, wings fanning; the numbers ride the captions
shots.motion_reason: slow drift across the comb keeps the colony's motion alive without cuts
shots.transition_reason: cut to the capped-cell macro for the defense layers

subject_contract.expected_subject: worker honeybees on a honeycomb frame, some fanning wings, hexagonal cells filled with honey
forbidden: a single giant bee portrait only

one_second.relationship: the fanning colony — evaporation as labour

shots.purpose: The vault itself: capped hexagonal cells — layered chemistry underneath
shots.claim: honey's acidity plus trace hydrogen peroxide add antibacterial layers
shots.evidence: extreme macro plate: hexagonal cells, wax caps, glistening honey
shots.motion_reason: macro drift: the geometry carries the stillness
shots.transition_reason: cut to the type card for the blunt statement

subject_contract.expected_subject: extreme macro of hexagonal honeycomb cells, some capped with pale beeswax, honey glistening inside

one_second.relationship: the capped hexagons — a sealed vault

shots.purpose: State the claim bluntly: the type IS the visual
shots.claim: honey resists spoilage on archaeological timescales
shots.evidence: full-frame type card: IT DOESN'T DIE
shots.transition_reason: cut to the tomb for the payoff

subject_contract.expected_subject: a full-frame typographic card: IT DOESN'T DIE with a small supporting line

shots.purpose: Land the payoff: the jar in the dark, sealed by its own chemistry
shots.claim: honey's stability is intrinsic chemistry, not storage
shots.evidence: amphora of honey glowing in a torchlit tomb
shots.motion_reason: slow drift to rest — the strongest composition holds

subject_contract.expected_subject: an ancient clay amphora glowing in a torchlit dark stone tomb
required: clay amphora or jar as focal subject

one_second.relationship: the kept jar — three thousand years of dark
